name: Iron Sage Binding Ground
summary: Iron Sage Binding Ground is a binding ground on the Mortal Plains, and iron-rich worked ground draws it and unworked ground never does, so the sage is always sitting on somebody's deposit. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Storm Phoenix Binding Ground
summary: Storm Phoenix Binding Ground is a binding ground on the Mortal Plains, and it needs an open sky and a rising current, which is why three of its grounds are on tiers where elemental law is unspent and the fire never actually takes. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Void Serpent Binding Ground
summary: Void Serpent Binding Ground is a binding ground on the Mortal Plains, and it follows water that has just gone somewhere else, which is why its grounds sit on the flood line rather than the bank. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Iron Titan Domain
summary: Iron Titan Domain is a forge ground on the Mortal Plains, and it is the slag of a spent seam - the only ground in the setting where a creature is made entirely out of what a mine left behind. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Void Leviathan Domain

name: Ironhide Bear Domain
summary: Ironhide Bear Domain is a creature range on the Mortal Plains, and it is the only bear here whose hide is armour, and it ranges the herb belt it is defending - so the belt has to be defended twice. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Storm Hawk Domain
summary: Storm Hawk Domain is a creature range on the Mortal Plains, and it hunts the updraught off hot worked ground, so it follows the seams rather than the scrub. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Venom Serpent Domain
summary: Venom Serpent Domain is a creature range on the Mortal Plains, and it lives in wet ground that only exists during the flood, so its range is measured in weeks a year. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Bitter Scrub
summary: The only ground on the Mortal Plains where herb_common grows, and so the tier's only medicine, dye and calories. It is worth fighting over because the same plant is medicine, feed and famine, the scrub cannot be fenced around a slow crop, and a bad grazing year is a medical shortage before it is a hunger.

attributes.regrowth_limited_by: grazing pressure, not by weather; nothing here is seasonally dormant because elemental law is unspent
attributes.fencing: impossible at the scrub's scale; a fence is a hole in the commons and is treated as one
attributes.why_it_is_the_tier's_pressure_point: a mortal body's only dependable remedy is grown on ground that livestock would rather have

name: Blood Refining Trial
summary: The Body Integration opening of the Body ladder, which refines the practitioner's own frame, held at the Cairn Field on the Mortal Plains: everything taken apart has to be reassembled on one site, so the ring is wide and unbroken. It exists because a three-imprint world cannot spend the slots a higher band needs, and it is the one tier that licenses nobody to attempt them, so every practitioner on this ring is a visitor.

name: Bone Refining Trial
summary: The Core Formation opening of the Body ladder, which refines the practitioner's own frame, held at the Cairn Field on the Mortal Plains: the first closed centre wants a hard floor and no resonance, so it is cut into stone. It exists because fifteen imprints over three layers is the only budget that can host a self larger than its container, and these are the only attempts that have ever needed one.

name: Organ Tempering Trial

name: Cairn Field
summary: The ring holding every mortal-band breakthrough from realms one to nine, on the one tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one. It exists because those nine trials are the only thing on the plains anyone would walk far to watch, so a tier with no practitioners and no export is sustained entirely by spectators - and the gate fees are the only tax the plains can actually collect.

attributes.spectator_economy: the crowd is the only export a resource-poor tier has, so the ring is held for gate fees rather than for teaching
attributes.who_uses_it: visitors from a tier that does license humanoids

name: Cloudshelf Sea
summary: The spirit tier's inland sea, with a coastline that holds its shape because spatial law is written here and a tide that keeps time because temporal law is. It matters as the setting's first hard edge: everywhere below this tier a border is a claim that can be argued, and here it is water that drowns you, which gives the quarrel a form no argument dissolves.

attributes.why_stable: spatial law is written at this tier, so the shelf holds its shape instead of behaving like the Hollow Measure
attributes.clock: the Tidemark season, because elemental and temporal law are both written
attributes.conflict_shape: two shores with a hard edge between them; neither can claim the water and neither can leave it

summary: Iron Monarch Domain is a seat on the Mortal Plains, and it sits on the spent seam's last standing face, which is the only worked ground on the plains with a wall. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Storm Sovereign Domain
summary: Storm Sovereign Domain is a seat on the Mortal Plains, and it is on the cairn field's open ground at the crest of the only weather cycle the plains have, which is not a season and does not keep to one. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Void Emperor Domain
summary: Void Emperor Domain is a seat on the Mortal Plains, and it is on the stair, because the stair is the only road in the setting whose position can be described the same way twice. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Terra Domain
summary: Terra Domain is a working elemental ground on the Spirit Peaks, where an elemental technique has a substrate to act on because this tier writes elemental law. It exists as the answer to geography.elemental_mortal_domain and geography.elemental_spirit_domain: the same technique fails absolutely on those two and works here, which is what makes the difference between an unspent law and a licensed one into a place worth walking to.

name: Aether Domain
summary: Aether Domain is a working elemental ground on the Immortal Court, where an elemental technique has a substrate to act on because this tier writes elemental law. It exists as the answer to geography.elemental_mortal_domain and geography.elemental_spirit_domain: the same technique fails absolutely on those two and works here, which is what makes the difference between an unspent law and a licensed one into a place worth walking to.

summary: Gale Domain is a working elemental ground on the Immortal Court, where an elemental technique has a substrate to act on because this tier writes elemental law. name: Ember Domain
summary: Ember Domain is a dead elemental ground on the Mortal Plains: a site built to prove that fire or tide can be used here, where elemental law is unspent and the proof is that nothing happens. It exists because an unwritten law does not weaken a technique, it removes it - so an elemental technique runs at full strength and produces nothing, and this is the place the setting keeps the record of having learned that the hard way.

name: Tide Domain
summary: Tide Domain is a dead elemental ground on the Spirit Peaks: a site built to prove that fire or tide can be used here, where elemental law is unspent and the proof is that nothing happens. It exists because an unwritten law does not weaken a technique, it removes it - so an elemental technique runs at full strength and produces nothing, and this is the place the setting keeps the record of having learned that the hard way.

name: Prism Domain
summary: Prism Domain is a working elemental ground on the Transcendent Realm, where an elemental technique has a substrate to act on because this tier writes elemental law. It exists as the answer to geography.elemental_mortal_domain and geography.elemental_spirit_domain: the same technique fails absolutely on those two and works here, which is what makes the difference between an unspent law and a licensed one into a place worth walking to.

name: Ember Ley
summary: The first ground in the setting where fire is simply fire: an elemental seam licensed because this tier writes elemental law and writes it twice. It matters because the two lower tiers left elemental law unspent, so an Emberblood affinity and every elemental technique ran at full strength and produced nothing - the same technique works here, and that asymmetry draws every fire practitioner in the setting to one valley.

attributes.contrast: geography.elemental_mortal_domain and geography.elemental_spirit_domain are the same attempt at a lower tier and produced nothing
attributes.attracts: every fire-affinity practitioner in the setting, none of whom is Dao-bound to this tier
attributes.access_from: the court's terraces and the stair; the ley is inland and open
attributes.the_valuation: a body at full elemental strength here is worth more than the same body anywhere below it, so the ley prices people rather than goods

name: Exhausted Seam
summary: The worked-out face on the Mortal Plains: forty years of cutting down to stone that pays nothing, with the spoil heap still standing on the ore that is gone. It matters because spoil does not disperse where spatial law is unspent, so exhaustion is visible from outside and a resource can be seen to have been spent out rather than suspected to have been.

attributes.waste_behaviour: does not disperse; the heap has grown in place for four decades
attributes.what_the_spoil_blocks: the seam's floor, so the working face cannot advance until the heap is moved, and moving it is the only remaining ore-costly job on the plains
attributes.why_it_is_a_symbol: it is the setting's clearest evidence that a resource can end, which every later scarcity argument is measured against

name: Flame Valley
summary: The one valley where fire does what fire is for: a cleft on the Spirit Peaks where elemental law is written, so every fire technique that failed at full strength below this tier works here. It exists because elemental law is unspent at the lower bands, so the valley is the first ground where an Emberblood affinity is an asset rather than a full-strength ability with nothing to act on.

name: Fragment Ring
summary: The transcendent-band trial ring, realms twenty-eight through thirty, standing on the Fragmentshelf where the ground is itself a broken law. It exists because a top-tier breakthrough is arithmetic rather than combat, and broken law is the only substrate that can host a self larger than its container - so three attempts have ever been possible here and fewer have ever been survived.

attributes.substrate: broken law; the only ground in the setting not trying to contain a self larger than its body
attributes.attempts_ever_survived: fewer than the three the band allows
attributes.least_permanent: the substrate cures while it is being used

name: Fragmentshelf
summary: The shelf where dao_fragment is cut: ground that is itself a broken piece of a law, workable only while the break is fresh. It matters because fragments cure as they decay and a cured fragment is void crystal, so the tier's two resources are two stages of one wound - the shelf is worked hardest by whoever knows it will be worthless in a generation and fought over hardest by whoever does not.

attributes.workable_window: while the break is fresh; there is no way to slow curing
attributes.deadline_economy: value falls with time, so holding the shelf without holding a buyer is holding a liability
attributes.the_top_tier_trilemma: the ground is the substrate, so the trial ring has to stand on it, so the ring and the mine compete for the same square

name: Gale Pass
summary: The single crossing of the Sixfold Ridge, and the reason the ridge is a border instead of a wall. It matters because the spirit tier writes spatial and temporal law, so a pass can be surveyed, closed and reopened on a schedule - making it the setting's first choke point, and the only supply route to both the jade cleft and Flame Valley.

attributes.why_schedulable_matters: a pass that can be surveyed can be closed and reopened on a published date, so the holder sets the rhythm of everyone downstream
attributes.the_toll_mechanism: a crossing window set by the Tidemark season, not by the holder's preference, which makes the toll defensible and the schedule not
attributes.who_loses_if_it_closes: the jade workers and the fire practitioners, who have no alternative route

name: The Hollow Measure
summary: The condition that makes the Mortal Plains impossible to survey: spatial law is unspent there, so distance is not conserved and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed. It matters because a border nobody can measure is a border somebody keeps taking, and every claim on the plains is settled by leaving a marker standing rather than by counting how far away it is.

attributes.signature: one of the three absence signatures: no process runs on it, so nothing keeps distance consistent
attributes.settlement_rule: possession is proven by a marker standing, never by a measurement of where it stands
attributes.cost_to_a_traveller: a party that leaves and returns reports a different distance each time, so the stair has to be the repeatable road rather than the plain
attributes.why_it_matters_downstream: no tax boundary, no land deed and no march order on the plains can be enforced by measurement, so every institution here is built on custom instead

name: Immortal Court
summary: The third tier's anchor: a high district of cut terraces over the Ember Ley and the Starmetal Scar, worked by humanoids and elementals. It exists because ten law slots over six groups leaves four duplicate imprints and a duplicate needs somewhere to sit, so this is the first tier with a second layer - and the surplus law rises through the district rather than being argued about above it.

name: Ironhead Flats
summary: The last unworked iron on the Mortal Plains, covering the deposit the Exhausted Seam was cut out of, and the only reason anyone settles ground that cannot be measured. It is worth holding because a resource with a visible end is what turns a plain into a country: the flats are the claim, the seam is the spending, and the argument is over which side of them a household may live on.

attributes.settlement_rule: there is no legal right to the flats; there is only the working face, and holding the face holds the claim
attributes.pressure: the flats are only worth holding while the seam is being worked, which makes every resident a temporary occupier by construction

name: Jade Cleft
summary: The far side of the Sixfold Ridge, where the jade seam runs in a narrow cold cleft no road reaches except through the Gale Pass. It matters because jade holds qi, so the cleft is the spirit tier's best refinement ground and its worst farming ground - a resource nobody can settle near, settleable nowhere, and reachable only through a door somebody else holds.

attributes.quality: holds qi, so the cleft is the tier's best refinement ground
attributes.agriculture: none; the cleft will not grow a crop
attributes.mining_problem: the seam is a gradient, not a pit - see ecology.jade_seam_draft
attributes.conflict_shape: whoever holds the pass claims the cleft by controlling supply, and whoever works the cleft claims the pass by refusing to be supplied

name: Ember Vault
summary: Ember Vault is a vault on the Mortal Plains, and the vault is cut into the heap itself, so its doors are spoil that has never moved. It exists because dead ground is where the setting keeps its records.

name: Storm Crypt
summary: Storm Crypt is a vault on the Mortal Plains, and the crypt is in the one place on the plains where a fixed record cannot be kept, which is either the worst site for a library or the safest. It exists because dead ground is where the setting keeps its records.

summary: Thunder Crane Domain is a inscription ground on the Spirit Peaks, and it is at the pass in the season the gale is worst, which is also the season nobody wants to cross. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Sixfold Ridge
summary: The range the Spirit Peaks are the name of: one wall carrying spirit stone and jade ore in the same bedding, folded six times. It is worth fighting over because the two deposits are one geological accident, so every claim on stone is a claim on jade and every claim on jade is a claim on the only pass over the ridge.

attributes.why_no_single_owner: the two deposits are one geological event, so a claim on either implies a claim on the other and the claims cannot be separated without re-cutting the ridge

name: Sixth Seat Grounds
summary: The spirit-band trial ring, realms ten through eighteen, cut into the Spirit Peaks where spirit stone is worked and the qi density is highest. It exists because all six law groups are written here, so a breakthrough can be scheduled to a qi tide instead of merely attempted - which means a trial that only succeeds at a crest can be shut on the day it is not due.

attributes.conflict_with_the_quarry: cutting stone and testing practitioners compete for the same density measurement

name: Spirit Peaks
summary: The second tier's anchor: one folded ridge carrying spirit stone and jade ore in the same bedding. It exists because six law slots is the first budget that can hold all six law groups, so this is where a coast holds its shape, a season keeps to a cycle and a distance means the same thing twice - the first tier where a border is a line rather than a claim.

name: Spiritscar Quarry
summary: The worked face in the Sixfold Ridge where spirit stone is cut, and the evidence for the Density Ceiling because it is a hole you can stand in and see the end of. It matters because a quarry is the only institution that measures a world instead of praising it, and the answer has been falling for three generations - which is why whoever benefits from the ceiling wants the hole shut.

attributes.measures: how much spirit stone the ridge has left per unit of ground worked
attributes.institutional_role: the only record of the tier's qi density that anybody can verify, because verification means digging
attributes.load_bearing_claim: history.era_the_sixth_seat requires spirit stone and jade ore, and they exist nowhere else

name: Starmetal Scar
summary: Where star metal surfaces in the Immortal Court: a wound that keeps healing because this tier runs at five to fifty times a slower world's clock. It matters because a resource that cannot be exhausted cannot be monopolised either, so the scar is indefensible ground everyone must keep using, and the only durable claim on it is over the approach rather than the metal.

attributes.regeneration: continuous; faster than extraction at the authored 5.0-50.0 time flow
attributes.why_not: supply is guaranteed and untied to any one party, so holding the scar buys a flow and not a monopoly
attributes.the_real_contested_object: the approach roads and the assay floor, not the seam

name: Earth Bloom Domain
summary: Earth Bloom Domain is a closed bond-assay ground on the Spirit Peaks: a bounded site where pact terms are measured and, when a term fails, contained. It exists because a binding is only measurable where the far party cannot leave between the offer and the outcome, so the containment is the ground rather than a ward - which is exactly why every holder wants it shut and every holder of the neighbouring crossing wants it open.

name: Heaven Bloom Domain
summary: Heaven Bloom Domain is a closed bond-assay ground on the Immortal Court: a bounded site where pact terms are measured and, when a term fails, contained. It exists because a binding is only measurable where the far party cannot leave between the offer and the outcome, so the containment is the ground rather than a ward - which is exactly why every holder wants it shut and every holder of the neighbouring crossing wants it open.

summary: Mortal Veil Domain is a closed bond-assay ground on the Mortal Plains: a bounded site where pact terms are measured and, when a term fails, contained. name: Transcendent Radiance Domain
summary: Transcendent Radiance Domain is a closed bond-assay ground on the Transcendent Realm: a bounded site where pact terms are measured and, when a term fails, contained. It exists because a binding is only measurable where the far party cannot leave between the offer and the outcome, so the containment is the ground rather than a ward - which is exactly why every holder wants it shut and every holder of the neighbouring crossing wants it open.

name: Terrace of Nine Seats
summary: Nine cut terraces on the Immortal Court's high ground, each sized for one office, and the ground the Nine Empty Seats are observed on. It matters because the vacancies are physical: a seat nobody has ever filled is an engraved absence, visible from the lower district, and the whole district is organised around the argument about who steps into it.

attributes.form: each terrace is cut to one office and shaped to forbid more than one occupant
attributes.legibility: visible from the lower district, which is what makes the vacancy a political fact rather than a private one
attributes.why_mind_dao_holds_it: mind Dao is native to the transcendent tier and holds both of its districts, so the top tier's politics are conducted from below its own home

name: Terrace Ring
summary: The immortal-band trial ring, realms nineteen through twenty-seven, on the court's upper ground above the Ember Ley. It exists because this tier runs at five to fifty times a slower clock, so a failed breakthrough injures the ground as well as the body - which makes the ring the only place in the setting where past attempts are still legible on the rock.

attributes.scarring: a failed breakthrough injures the ground as well as the body, because this tier runs at 5.0-50.0x time
attributes.record_integrity: the scars cannot be edited by whoever lost them, so this is the setting's only trustworthy arena record

name: Third Layer Hold
summary: The Transcendent Realm's third layer, where fifteen imprints over three layers leave nine surplus imprints with nowhere to go but up. It matters because at this tier the surplus is the place: nothing grows, nothing recovers, nothing is cheap, so access is a discipline rather than a journey and the tier's entire hierarchy is a queue for it.

attributes.the_place_is_the_surplus: at this tier the duplicate imprints are the ground, so the hierarchy is physical
attributes.regrowth: none; nothing here is renewed at any rate
attributes.access: discipline, not distance; the layer can be held by a will rather than a road
attributes.why_the_tier_is_built: 15 imprints over 3 layers exceed what one will holds, so this ground was assembled by merging rather than reached

name: The Tidemark
summary: The anchored season that decides when the Cloudshelf Sea can be crossed and when the Gale Pass is safe, which this tier can have only because elemental law is written here. It matters because a calendar is the first form of wealth: whoever reads the Tidemark sets the shipping dates, and a shipping date is obeyed by people who never heard of its author.

attributes.why_here_only: elemental law governs seasonal cycles and is unspent at the mortal tier, so below this line the weather recurs without anything holding it to a cycle
attributes.the_soft_power_mechanism: publishing the window is cheaper than enforcing it, and the party that publishes it is the party everybody plans around
attributes.countermeasure: keeping a second season table kept by someone who does not hold either crossing

name: The Tier Stair
summary: The one graded route out of the Mortal Plains and the only departure the Peak Ascent ever used. It exists because distance is not conserved on the plains, so a road that measures itself is the only repeatable departure there - which makes it the setting's first portable institution and the only piece of the mortal tier with a constituency on four tiers.

attributes.why_it_is_the_only_one: unmeasured ground cannot be re-walked to the same place, so a road that measures itself is the only repeatable departure from the Hollow Measure
attributes.what_it_carries: people, iron, and the only people who can attempt a mortal-band trial
attributes.who_most_wants_it_closed: everyone on the plains who is not a practitioner, because the tier licenses no humanoid and the stair is the only door practitioners arrive through
attributes.why_it_is_one_way: spatial law is unspent on the plains, so the return is a walk whose distance cannot be established; arrival is repeatable and departure is not

name: Abyssal Serpent Domain
summary: Abyssal Serpent Domain is a reading ground on the Transcendent Realm, and it is in the cold depth under the cured crystal, where the supply grows and nothing else does. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Cinder Tiger Domain
summary: Cinder Tiger Domain is a reading ground on the Transcendent Realm, and it is on the freshest cut, because a fresh break still throws heat and a cured one does not. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Gilded Crane Domain
summary: Gilded Crane Domain is a reading ground on the Transcendent Realm, and it is in the third layer, where nothing renews - so nothing there is ever in a hurry and everything there is late. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Iron Bull Totem Domain
summary: Iron Bull Totem Domain is a pillar ground on the Immortal Court, and it stands on the scar's outcrops, which is the only exposed metal in the tier that has not been cut yet. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Jade Serpent Totem Domain
summary: Jade Serpent Totem Domain is a pillar ground on the Immortal Court, and it lives on the duplicate-imprint shelf, because something has to live in the difference between two writings of the same law. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Stone Guardian Totem Domain
summary: Stone Guardian Totem Domain is a pillar ground on the Immortal Court, and it stands at the nine empty seats, in stone that was cut and shaped to forbid more than one occupant. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Transcendent Realm
summary: The top tier's anchor: a shattered shelf of broken law where dao_fragment cures into void crystal, held under a three-layer imprint set. It matters because fifteen imprints over three layers leave nine surplus imprints, and nine surplus is a load rather than a resource - so this ground was assembled by merging, never grown into, and it holds the setting's only door between worlds.

name: Frost Hermit Domain
summary: Frost Hermit Domain is a cache on the Transcendent Realm, and it is in the expanse, where nothing grows and therefore nothing needs anything, which is the only place in the setting it can want nothing. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Gilded Beetle Domain
summary: Gilded Beetle Domain is a cache on the Immortal Court, and it is in the unworked star metal, on the only part of the scar nobody has cut because there is no assay for it yet. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Iron Sage Treasure Cache
summary: Iron Sage Treasure Cache is a cache on the Spirit Peaks, and iron-rich worked ground draws it and unworked ground never does, so the sage is always sitting on somebody's deposit. It exists because a holding here is a place somebody can hold, not a place the creature is.

name: Void Expanse
summary: The cured end of the shelf, where dao_fragment has finished breaking down into void crystal in a quantity no lower tier's physics can hold. It matters because curing is one-way and runs at ten to a hundred times a slower clock, so the expanse grows every period - making it the only resource in the setting nobody can corner, and its holders the only people with nothing to gain from a war.

attributes.supply: monotonic; grows every period and cannot be slowed
attributes.why: a guaranteed and unbounded supply means there is nothing to be gained by controlling the ground
attributes.relation_to_shelf: the same ground at a later stage; see geography.fragmentshelf
attributes.the_paradox: the top tier's scarcest-looking region holds its least scarce resource

name: Widow Run
summary: The Mortal Plains' single watercourse, dry most of the year, full for weeks, and moving its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it. It matters because temporal law is written here at 0.5-2.0 with qi at the floor, so the flood is the only clock the plains own, and every settlement on the run is revocable once a generation.

attributes.flow: one flood per year; dry the rest
attributes.bed_movement: enough between floods to relocate a settlement
attributes.the_plains_only_clock: temporal law written at 0.5-2.0 with qi_law at the floor makes the flood the sole cycle available
attributes.settlement_rule: no settlement is permanent; the choice is near-water or above-water, and near-water wins because the scrub does not grow without it
attributes.conflict_shape: upstream versus downstream, where upstream can simply not irrigate and let the flood settle the argument
